
### mailbox model 



* <i>mailbox</i> abstraction: send/receive messages
 

::: {.r-stack}

![](/network/texfig/mailbox-model.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 width=1000px fig-alt="machine A runs Send(B, 'Hello'). This sends 'B: Hello' to the network, represented by a cloud. The network then sends 'B: Hello' to B. On B, Recv() returns 'Hello'."}

![](/network/texfig/mailbox-model.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 width=1000px }

![](/network/texfig/mailbox-model.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 width=1000px fig-alt="On machine B, there is also a queue."}

![](/network/texfig/mailbox-model.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4 width=1000px fig-alt="On machine A, there is a queue before the output to the network."}

:::

::: {.myoverbox .vlow .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1}

*  A sends "letter" to B
*  "envelope" tells network it's addressed to B
*  data in this example: Hello

:::

::: {.myoverbox .vlow .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3}

*  the network provides "best effort" at getting message to B
   *  Internet-like networks: no gaurentees

:::

::: {.myoverbox .vlow .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3}

*  queues ("outgoing mailbox") of messages at sender A
*  things sending program has 'sent', but haven't made it to network

:::

::: {.myoverbox .vlow .fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=4}

*  queues ("incoming mailbox") of messages at receiver B
*  things machine B has received, but not passed to program

:::




### connections over mailboxes  {.smaller}


* real Internet: mailbox-style communication 

   * send ‘‘letters’’ (packets) to particular mailboxes
   * have ‘‘envelope’’ (header) saying where they go
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* ‘‘best-effort’’ 

   * no guarantee on order, when received
   * no guarantee on <i>if</i> received

* sockets implemented on top of this
